If you cannot describe what done looks like, you have not delegated, you have handed off your worry.
Generic praise tells someone you noticed them. Specific praise tells them you noticed the work.
An open door that is never actually open teaches people to stop knocking.
A meeting with no decision at the end was a status update wearing a calendar invite.
If you only correct people in private, the team never learns what the standard actually is.
People do not trust you because you are always right. They trust you because you say when you are wrong.
A team with eleven priorities has none, it just has eleven things nobody finished.
The manager who redoes every piece of work is training the team to stop trying.
